items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: I knew Papin, Tata Guines, you know etcetera etcetera when I was a boy.

ctx.x: How did you know what to do with a swing groove, and did you get the feeling that you were kind of intruding on the goings on?

No man. Maybe it’s because I listened to so much American music as a kid. I just – oh, [scats] it’s timbao – it’s what we call timbao in Afro-Cuban, but just swing it. That’s all it is. You know. But at that time I had never heard of Chano Pozo, I had never heard of any of this. I didn’t know anything man. I really didn’t – of any of the – I started finding out who – I never heard of Mongo Santamaria, I had never heard of Tito Puente, I had never heard of Patato Valdes. These are guys that had left. I knew Papin,…
I bet you had some revelations along the way. I mean at that time there was some hit records by those fellas. Like “Watermelon Man” and some of the more accessible tunes.
